item.title: NPR: California voters defeat billionaire tax proposal that divided Democrats
item.description: The novel proposal would have charged billionaires a one-time 5% tax on most of their overall wealth, including their ownership in companies.

item.title: PBS NewsHour: Nvidia's Jensen Huang faces scrutiny over alleged affair with Chinese spy
item.description: Lawmakers, investors and tech leaders are assessing bombshell revelations about Nvidia founder and CEO Jensen Huang. Huang admitted to an affair with a woman accused of being a Chinese spy. Nvidia designs chips and processors that power artificial intelligence and underpin much of the enormous investment in the industry. William Brangham reports.

item.title: PBS NewsHour: What China stands to gain from Nvidia's CEO's alleged affair with spy
item.description: To discuss the national security risks of Nvidia's CEO having an affair with a possible foreign intelligence agent, Amna Nawaz spoke with Christopher Johnson. He spent 20 years in the U.S. intelligence community focusing on China. He now runs his own consulting firm, China Strategies Group.

item.title: PBS NewsHour: Citing government pressure, Russia's top independent newspaper closes its office after three decades
item.description: Novaya Gazeta was the last major independent media outlet critical of the Kremlin that remained active in Russia.

item.title: PBS NewsHour: How the Nvidia revelations could ripple through the AI industry and global economy
item.description: To discuss the national security risks of Nvidia's CEO having an affair with a possible foreign intelligence agent, Amna Nawaz spoke with Christopher Johnson. He spent 20 years in the U.S. intelligence community focusing on China. He now runs his own consulting firm, China Strategies Group.

item.title: PBS NewsHour: News Wrap: Supreme Court allows border wall construction in Big Bend
item.description: In our news wrap Monday, the Supreme Court is allowing the Trump administration to continue building a section of border wall in a remote part of Texas that includes Big Bend National Park, Russia and Ukraine exchanged long-range strikes ahead of U.S. brokered talks and French officials are blaming Iran for a massive cyberattack on supermarket refrigerators.

item.title: PBS NewsHour: What we know — and what we don't — as Nvidia investigates an alleged spy plot involving its CEO
item.description: Many questions remain unanswered. But the scandal is already bringing turmoil to California-based Nvidia, whose high-end chips have emerged as the leading building blocks for artificial intelligence.

item.title: PBS NewsHour: Hegseth faces impeachment push as Congress returns to Washington
item.description: There were some new faces on Capitol Hill on Monday as incoming lawmakers arrived for their orientation. But for the current House and Senate, it was back to business. They began one final stretch before the GOP loses its control of Congress in January. Rep. Thomas Massie of Kentucky moved to force a vote to impeach Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth. Lisa Desjardins reports.

item.title: PBS NewsHour: South Carolina wins give Democrats hope to expand reach in Deep South
item.description: One of the stunning upsets of last week's election was in South Carolina, where Democrat Annie Andrews defeated incumbent Republican Darline Graham in the Senate race. That wasn't the only Democratic victory in the deep red state. Democrats also flipped a House seat and flipped 10 seats in the state house. Geoff Bennett discussed more with South Carolina's Democratic Party chair, Christale Spain.

item.title: PBS NewsHour: Judge's ruling could clear the way for Lindsay Clancy to be tried again in the deaths of her three kids
item.description: Clancy's defense team had asked the court to end the case based on an unusual argument that the judge shouldn't have declared a mistrial in September when jurors were unable to reach a unanimous verdict.

item.title: PBS NewsHour: Tamara Keith and Amy Walter on how Trump will govern after the blue wave
item.description: NPR's Tamara Keith and Amy Walter of the Cook Political Report with Amy Walter join Amna Nawaz to discuss the latest political news, including President Trump sending mixed messages about how he plans to govern for the remainder of his term after Democrats' historic wins in the midterms, the effort to impeach Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth and the battle for party leadership in Congress.

item.title: PBS NewsHour: Gaza students work toward college degrees after years of war and displacement
item.description: In Gaza, more than half a million students are back in school after three years. The picture has been equally bleak for post-secondary education, which has been virtually non-existent since the start of the war in Gaza. Special correspondent Fred de Sam Lazaro reports on an unusual partnership trying to fill part of the void.

item.title: PBS NewsHour: Judge dismisses case from Dolly Parton's manager alleging her nephew threatened her estate
item.description: A Tennessee judge on Monday dismissed a case brought by Dolly Parton 's longtime manager who was seeking an injunction against her nephew and head of security, alleging he had threatened her estate and its employees.

item.title: PBS NewsHour: WATCH: Trump says FBI is looking into Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang's affair with alleged Chinese agent
item.description: President Donald Trump said Monday that Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang should not worry about the FBI looking into his affair with a woman alleged to be a Chinese government agent.

item.title: NPR: France accuses Iran of cyber 'sabotage' in fridge attacks
item.description: France says Iranian military hackers took over refrigeration controllers at around 700 different retail sites last month, turning up temperatures in the middle of the night and spoiling millions of dollars' worth of food.

item.title: PBS NewsHour: Democrats plan to use new power to rein in Trump's education agenda. But their tools are limited
item.description: Democrats in Congress are gearing up to challenge President Donald Trump's education policies, including the dismantling of the U.S. Education Department.

item.title: PBS NewsHour: California's fifth consecutive Catholic governor exemplifies the faith's deep roots
item.description: Xavier Becerra's recent election as California governor highlights the state's unique blend of Catholicism and progressive politics.

item.title: PBS NewsHour: France blames Iran for last month's cyberattack on supermarket fridges
item.description: France on Monday blamed Iran for last month's massive cyberattack on supermarket fridges, summoned the Iranian ambassador and said it would seek European sanctions against those responsible for the attack.

item.title: NPR: Stephen Miller is now chief of staff. What does that mean for Trump?
item.description: NPR's Sacha Pfeiffer speaks with Chris Whipple, an expert on White House chiefs of staff who has written extensively about Susie Wiles, about Trump's appointment of Stephen Miller.

item.title: NPR: Thomas Massie files articles of impeachment against Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth
item.description: The articles accuse Hegseth of "high crimes and misdemeanors," including for waging war against Iran in violation of the War Powers Resolution.

item.title: PBS NewsHour: WATCH: Smog blankets New Delhi after Diwali celebrations
item.description: New Delhi was blanketed by hazy smog Monday after a weekend of Diwali celebrations.

item.title: PBS NewsHour: WATCH LIVE: Rep. Massie speaks after filing Hegseth impeachment resolution
item.description: Rep. Thomas Massie moved Monday to force a vote to impeach Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth, setting the stage for a dramatic vote on whether to remove one of the Trump administration's most prominent figures following sweeping election losses.

item.title: PBS NewsHour: Even after the midterm rout of Trumpism, the world struggles to trust America
item.description: The U.S. midterm rout of President Donald Trump's stewardship doesn't mean the world trusts America again.

item.title: PBS NewsHour: In memoir, Biden says Trump should carry the weight of Jan. 6 riots 'to his grave'
item.description: The first excerpt of "Promise Me, America" was published Monday by The Atlantic. The full memoir is set for a Nov. 17 release.

item.title: PBS NewsHour: WATCH: Hegseth announces he will hold news conference on impeachment threat to defend his record
item.description: Facing an expected impeachment resolution in Congress, Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth said he's eager to litigate the policy choices that he and President Donald Trump have made in Iran and Venezuela.

item.title: PBS NewsHour: Democrats plan to challenge Trump's fossil fuel agenda and push clean energy to lower bills
item.description: Some Democrats are promising to push for more clean energy to help tackle rising energy costs when they take control of Congress in January, though President Donald Trump says he will use his veto power aggressively.

item.title: PBS NewsHour: WATCH LIVE: Senate returns to Capitol Hill days after Democrats win back control
item.description: The Senate on Monday is set to take up bipartisan legislation aimed at speeding up permitting reviews for data centers and other infrastructure projects, in the first major action since last week's election that soundly repudiated President Donald Trump and congressional Republicans.

item.title: PBS NewsHour: COP31 climate summit begins after disastrous year of extreme weather
item.description: orld leaders, delegates and climate activists on Monday kicked off talks in Turkey on curbing climate change, which in the last year has led to rising temperatures and deadly heat waves in Europe and beyond.

item.title: PBS NewsHour: Outdated power grids a major hurdle in renewable energy transition
item.description: Outdated power grids around the world are a major hurdle in the transition from fossil fuels to renewable energy. Older grids often can't absorb all the electricity generated by new solar and wind installations.

item.title: PBS NewsHour: Russia-Ukraine peace talks led by U.S. will look at security guarantees for both sides
item.description: The negotiations follow last month's localized truce around the Russian-occupied city of Oleshky in southern Ukraine that allowed the evacuation of some trapped residents and the delivery of desperately needed humanitarian supplies.

item.title: PBS NewsHour: Boosting healthcare and ending the Iran war are top of the to-do list for House Democrats once they have majority
item.description: The legislative flurry carries enormous stakes for Democrats as they seek to translate their sweeping victories in the midterms into achievements that deliver on their promises to lower the cost of living.

item.title: PBS NewsHour: Russia and Ukraine exchange strikes a day before U.S.-brokered talks are scheduled to begin
item.description: President Donald Trump mentioned in a "60 Minutes" interview that the two sides are "very close" to a deal.

item.title: PBS NewsHour: WATCH LIVE: House returns to Washington after blowout election for Democrats
item.description: Congress returns Monday to a changed Washington, the Democrats having trounced Republicans in the midterm elections, but with President Donald Trump doubling down on his political threats despite the landmark GOP losses.

item.title: PBS NewsHour: Russell Brand is sentenced to more than 10 years in prison for rape and sexual assault
item.description: A jury found him guilty of attacking four of six accusers, with allegations dating back to 2004.

item.title: PBS NewsHour: Trump says idea to make UFC's Dana White his press secretary 'just a little fun'
item.description: Trump does not currently have a press secretary after briefly giving the job to Katie Zacharia, who left the post after five days.

item.title: PBS NewsHour: WATCH LIVE: Hegseth speaks at the Naval War College as possible impeachment vote looms
item.description: An impeachment vote for Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth tops Congress' lame-duck agenda.

item.title: NPR: Palantir hires a former Democratic senator as it faces scrutiny in new Congress
item.description: The secretive software company has been accused of letting its powerful tools be used by the Trump administration to surveil Americans. Now it's hiring former Sen. Jon Tester to burnish its image.

item.title: PBS NewsHour: Trump says his deportation policy 'might have been too tough' for midterm voters
item.description: Trump said that he thinks he can work with Democrats in the new Congress on some kind of immigration deal.

item.title: PBS NewsHour: Deportation flight of Iranians from U.S. canceled at last minute, attorney says
item.description: The U.S. Department of Homeland Security refused to comment on the details of removal operations.

item.title: PBS NewsHour: Pope visits care home in Argentina for people with disabilities, renewing call to protect the vulnerable
item.description: Known as the "city of charity," it has been hit hard by President Javier Milei's austerity measures, which have severely affected healthcare and social services.

item.title: NPR: British comedian Russell Brand sentenced to over 10 years for rape and sexual assault
item.description: Russell Brand, who became a celebrity darling in the early 2000s, was found guilty on one count of rape and three counts of sexual assault in a case brought by six women.

item.title: PBS NewsHour: China dismisses claims of spy plot involving Nvidia CEO Huang as a smear campaign
item.description: In a routine news briefing Monday, a Chinese spokesperson rejected claims it used the woman as a spy.

item.title: PBS NewsHour: Nvidia investigates whether CEO Jensen Huang was targeted by Chinese spy when he had affair
item.description: The announcement came after Huang acknowledged to the board that he had been intimate with a business executive whom, according to The New York Times, U.S. intelligence determined was gathering information for Beijing.

item.title: NPR: Congress is back after GOP's midterm defeat. And, Trump appoints new chief of staff
item.description: Republicans have just weeks left of control of Congress. Here's what to expect. And, Trump has appointed Stephen Miller as his new chief of staff, signaling his readiness to confront his opposition.

item.title: NPR: After midterm losses, Trump makes changes to his inner circle
item.description: President Trump is shaking up his closest advisers after Democrats made huge gains in the midterm elections.

item.title: NPR: Democrats won big. Can they lower your grocery bill?
item.description: Affordability concerns were top of mind for voters heading into the midterms, as tariffs and the war in Iran drove up prices, including food costs. Now, Americans are expecting relief from Washington.

item.title: NPR: Supreme Court weighs effort to shield federal law enforcement as ICE complaints rise
item.description: The Supreme Court considers the case of a prisoner who suffered brutal injuries, only to be denied medical care behind bars. He wants to sue the prison nurse in a case that could change the law on holding federal officers accountable.

item.title: NPR: Congress is coming back to Washington. Here's what to expect
item.description: Lawmakers are coming back to Washington this week after the midterm elections. Republicans plan to finish work on several outstanding issues before Democrats take control of Congress in January.

item.title: NPR: Midterm results could complicate JD Vance's political future
item.description: Vice President JD Vance is looking to recast his political fortune after serving as the Trump administration's No. 2 while his party suffered a historic wipeout.

item.title: NPR: Democratic Sen. Chris Coons on his party's post-midterm priorities
item.description: NPR's Leila Fadel speaks to Democratic Sen. Chris Coons of Delaware about Democrats' congressional priorities after the midterms.

item.title: PBS NewsHour: Pope Leo arrives in Argentina and tells Milei that people, not the economy, should come first
item.description: Leo's visit to Argentina is by far the most politically delicate of his three-nation South American tour, and a place where Leo will also confront the complicated legacy of Argentine Pope Francis, who never returned home during his 12-year pontificate.

item.title: NPR: Trump staffing changes post-midterms signal he's battle ready
item.description: President Trump is making changes to his inner circle that signal how he may approach divided government.

item.title: NPR: How will Democrats approach foreign policy after their midterm win?
item.description: NPR's Rob Schmitz speaks with Thomas Wright, senior fellow at the Brookings Institution, about his piece in Foreign Affairs titled The Fight for the Future of Democratic Foreign Policy.

item.title: PBS NewsHour: Voters demanded economic relief. Trump and Democrats face tough choices on how to deliver
item.description: Trump, who campaigned on the idea that a Democratic victory in the midterms would trigger a 1929-style economic depression, has maintained that the economy is booming. Since his party lost in Tuesday's voting, he has claimed he is willing to work with Democrats in the House and Senate, though that's not something he has done much of in the past.

item.title: PBS NewsHour: Native American women made history in tribal, state and federal elections
item.description: Peggy Flanagan became the first Native American woman elected to the Senate, Deb Haaland the first to win a state governorship, and Crystalyne Curley the first to lead the Navajo Nation.

item.title: PBS NewsHour: Trump and his Justice Department stand defiant as Democrats ready an investigative blitz
item.description: Trump set the tone, declaring on social media that investigative requests already made by Democrats are "extortion at the highest level, and they should be held accountable."

item.title: PBS NewsHour: The Kremlin hopes the U.S. election shake-up won't shift Trump's negotiations on Ukraine
item.description: Asked if the election's outcome could stymie U.S. attempts to help negotiate a settlement between Moscow and Kyiv, Kremlin spokesperson Dmitry Peskov voiced hope that President Donald Trump will continue to pursue his peace efforts.

item.title: PBS NewsHour: Poles mourn rare mass killing as authorities say attacker had far-right views
item.description: The attack, which Poland's defense minister described as an "act of terror," happened on Saturday in the Main Square, in the heart of Krakow's Old Town. The square is a major tourist hub in the country's second-largest city.

item.title: PBS NewsHour: The midterms energized a powerful political constituency: abuse survivors
item.description: From Ohio Gov.-elect Amy Acton's victory to candidates accused of abuse withdrawing, advocates are calling this year's elections "a win for survivors."

item.title: PBS NewsHour: AP sources: Staff at U.S. center for AI safety are reporting to the White House, raising independence concerns
item.description: Officials with the Center for Advancing Innovation and Standards for Super Intelligence, or CAISSI, an independent division of the Commerce Department, recently were asked to informally report to an office of the White House.

item.title: PBS NewsHour: Collision between 2 trains in Egypt kills 7 and injures more than 100
item.description: Train derailments and crashes are common in Egypt, where the railway system which has a history of mismanagement and poor maintenance of equipment. In recent years, the government announced modernization initiatives to improve its railways.

item.title: PBS NewsHour: Floods bring rare relief to U.S. Southwest reservoirs as Lake Powell rises 20 feet
item.description: Storms in late October and early November sent torrents of water through normally small or dry creeks that overflowed their banks and flooded local communities.

item.title: NPR: No clear winner in New Zealand election, as leaders prepare for weeks of talks
item.description: Prime Minister Christopher Luxon, who will lead a caretaker government while negotiations take place, said: "I think everyone's over politics so let's all have a bit of a break for the next three weeks".

item.title: PBS NewsHour: Israel's president formally gives Eisenkot the first chance to form the next government
item.description: At the ceremony in Jerusalem, Eisenkot said he wanted a leadership that people can trust, that will act in the interests of the public and that represents all parts of society.

item.title: NPR: NPR's Moscow and Beijing correspondents discuss the reaction to U.S. elections abroad
item.description: The results of the U.S. midterms were closely followed overseas. NPR correspondents in Moscow and Beijing discuss how the elections are seen in the countries they cover.

item.title: NPR: Republican consultant discusses what went wrong and what's next for the GOP
item.description: NPR's Ayesha Rascoe speaks to Hogan Gidley, a Republican consultant and former White House Deputy Press Secretary during the first Trump administration, about the GOP's post-midterm strategy.

item.title: NPR: Historically red state legislatures have flipped. Here's what's on their agenda
item.description: Democrats made sweeping gains in state legislatures across the country. We look at North Carolina and Arizona to see what that could mean.

item.title: NPR: Week in politics: Democrats plan for the next Congress, Trump's new Chief of Staff
item.description: Democrats plans for the next Congress, where they'll hold significant majorities in both chambers. Meanwhile, President Trump signals his plans by promoting Stephen Miller as his new Chief of Staff.

item.title: NPR: How Gen Z voters helped fuel a blue wave for Democrats
item.description: Republicans made gains with young voters in 2024, but in this year's midterms Americans under 30 issued a strong rebuke of President Trump and his party, voting decisively for Democrats instead.

item.title: NPR: UFC's Dana White says he will meet with Trump Monday over offer to be White House press secretary
item.description: President Donald Trump said Saturday that he has offered the job of White House press secretary to his friend and UFC boss Dana White.

item.title: PBS NewsHour: What is Diwali, the Festival of Lights, and how is it celebrated?
item.description: The festival follows the Hindu lunar calendar, typically falling in late October or early November. This year, Diwali falls on Nov. 8.

item.title: NPR: Texas's 'Blue Tsunami' has former Texas congressman Beto O'Rourke 'over the moon'
item.description: NPR's Rob Schmitz speaks with former Texas congressman Beto O'Rourke about how past efforts by him and other Democrats helped the party win big in Texas in the midterms.

item.title: NPR: President of The Heritage Foundation looks ahead to the future of the GOP
item.description: Kevin Roberts, the president of the conservative think tank The Heritage Foundation, talks about the organization's priorities and hopes for the future of the Republican Party and its policies.

item.title: PBS NewsHour: Sen. Chris Murphy's stroke at 53 highlights a trend: Strokes among younger adults have risen
item.description: Researchers found that the stroke incidence rate among adults from 1993-94 nearly doubled in 2020, jumping from 33.90 cases per 100,000 people to 62.18 cases.

item.title: PBS NewsHour: Trump says he's asked UFC's Dana White to be his press secretary
item.description: Trump's social media post about the offer came as his White House is in a period of major transition and struggling with his party's deep losses in Tuesday's midterm elections.

item.title: PBS NewsHour: Israel's president taps opposition candidate Eisenkot to form a government, in setback for Netanyahu
item.description: Neither Eisenkot nor Netanyahu won a clear majority in the vote. But in marathon discussions with the president this week, representatives from most of Israel's main parties recommended Eisenkot be tasked with assembling a new government.

item.title: PBS NewsHour: Melania Trump and LSU announce a scholarship program for students who were in foster care
item.description: Trump and LSU secured more than $7 million in private donations to create an endowment fund for the scholarships, the White House said.

item.title: PBS NewsHour: Judge wants former U.S. attorney to investigate whether the government misled her in Trump golf case
item.description: The administration plans to close the East Potomac Golf Course and park on Nov. 15 with the intention of constructing a "World Class, championship-level golf course that is capable of hosting major events."

item.title: PBS NewsHour: With an ode to mate, Pope Leo urges faithful in Uruguay to build bridges of fraternity and faith
item.description: More than 30,000 people — many from Uruguay but also from neighboring Argentina and Brazil — had registered in advance to attend the service. The Vatican said Saturday that another 10,000 had attended, despite the morning rain.

item.title: PBS NewsHour: Scott Colom and Black Mississippians stand on the cusp of Senate history as vote count stretches on
item.description: The state is still tallying ballots that could make Colom the first Black senator from this Deep South state since post-Civil War Reconstruction.

item.title: PBS NewsHour: In his words: Stephen Miller is an immigration hardliner and a bombastic critic of Democrats
item.description: An outspoken defender of President Donald Trump's most far-reaching goals to remake government going back to his 2016 run for president, Miller is known for his harsh language and unapologetic bombast.

item.title: PBS NewsHour: Gunman opens fire in Polish city of Krakow, killing 6 people and injuring 15
item.description: The gunman, a Polish citizen, aimed at random people as he drove into the Main Square, a major tourist destination in the center of the city, Krakow police said.

item.title: NPR: Ousted Paraguayan president appears before prosecutors
item.description: Paraguayan President Santiago Peña was removed from office and placed on House arrest Friday. The Senate voted on his impeachment after the collapse of a state-affiliated bank.

item.title: PBS NewsHour: Paraguay's ousted president faces prosecutors after his removal over bank collapse
item.description: Paraguayan prosecutors on Friday ordered the arrest of Peña and former Central Bank chief Carlos Carvallo as part of a criminal investigation into alleged breach of trust and other offenses tied to the collapse of Ueno Bank.

item.title: PBS NewsHour: Justice Department drops bid to force California to set aside disputed ballots
item.description: The move comes days after Republicans' significant losses in the midterm elections and about a week before a scheduled hearing where a special master was slated to evaluate the accuracy of the list of alleged noncitizens.

item.title: NPR: How the new Senate majority shifts control over the federal judiciary
item.description: The change in the Senate's majority party means that starting Jan. 3, Democrats will run federal judicial appointments and may continue to until at least 2030.

item.title: NPR: GOP's lame-duck clock is ticking
item.description: The current Congress, under its Republican majorities, must address the National Defense Authorization Act and a government funding bill as Democrats wait to take over.

item.title: NPR: Border shift: Hispanic voters drive Texas' historic flip to blue
item.description: Once reliably a red state, Texas will turn deep blue following this week's midterms. One of the most notable shifts was along the Texas-Mexico border, where Hispanic voters had a big influence.

item.title: NPR: Week in Politics: Trump taps Miller for chief of staff; doubles down on Trumpism
item.description: President Trump's decision to make Stephen Miller his new chief of staff is a rebuke of the midterm results and a doubling-down on Trumpism.

item.title: NPR: Deb Haaland's New Mexico challenge
item.description: Deb Haaland is the first Native American governor of New Mexico. She faces big expectations and challenges, but also opportunities in a deep blue state with abundant petroleum revenue.

item.title: NPR: Defiance Mayor Mike McCann on how Republicans can regroup after midterm losses
item.description: Republicans were routed in the midterm elections. NPR's Scott Simon talks to Mike McCann, the Mayor of Defiance, Ohio, about how the Republican party can win back support.

item.title: NPR: An unexpected activist emerged to help block a $5 billion data center in Maryland
item.description: Thousands across the U.S. have gotten involved to oppose data centers. One is a Maryland woman who'd been evicted after a pay cut and became a leader of a community effort that blocked a vast project.

item.title: PBS NewsHour: What Trump picking Stephen Miller for chief of staff signals about his agenda
item.description: Trump has replaced White House chief of staff Susie Wiles with Stephen Miller, the hardline architect of his immigration agenda, after a crushing midterm defeat. Immigration, once a political strength for Trump, became a liability after two years of mass detentions, deportations and armed agents in U.S. cities. Miller's appointment signals a doubling down on Trump's agenda. Liz Landers reports.

item.title: PBS NewsHour: News Wrap: Judge blocks construction of Trump's triumphal arch for now
item.description: In our news wrap Friday, Trump's plans to build a massive triumphal arch near Arlington National Cemetery have been put on hold, two more top officials resigned from the Justice Department, residents along the Georgia-Tennessee border are returning home after record floodwaters receded, Pope Leo started his 12-day tour of Latin America, and Tesla will wind down production of its Cybertruck.

item.title: PBS NewsHour: What to know about a better-than-expected jobs report amid AI bubble concerns
item.description: Employers added 165,000 new jobs in October, according to a new government report. Job gains for August and September were revised upward as well, by a combined 84,000 jobs. That makes the last three months of the job market look better than expected, but it comes as questions grow about the sustainability of the AI boom. Amna Nawaz speaks with Diane Swonk, chief economist for KPMG, for more.

item.title: PBS NewsHour: Georgia Gov.-elect Bottoms reflects on historic victory and the path forward for Democrats
item.description: Georgia voters made history this week, electing Keisha Lance Bottoms as the state's first Democratic senator in more than two decades and the first-ever Black woman governor in the country. The former Atlanta mayor campaigned on lowering costs, expanding healthcare access and pushing back against the Trump administration. Geoff Bennett speaks with Gov.-elect Bottoms for more.

item.title: PBS NewsHour: Former Sen. Flake, outspoken Trump critic, on the GOP reckoning post-midterms
item.description: As Democrats celebrate their historic gains, Republicans are beginning to take stock of major upsets and what comes next for their party. Amna Nawaz speaks with former Arizona Sen. Jeff Flake, one of the most outspoken Republican critics of Trump during his first administration and the author of the 2017 book "The Conscience of a Conservative."

item.title: PBS NewsHour: Brooks and Capehart on Trump's White House shakeup and fallout from the midterms
item.description: David Brooks of The Atlantic and Jonathan Capehart of MS NOW join Geoff Bennett to discuss the week in politics, including Trump shaking up his White House leadership, deep divisions in the Republican Party and how Democrats are preparing to take control of Congress.

item.title: PBS NewsHour: Remembering Jay Rockefeller's life and legacy of public service
item.description: Jay Rockefeller, former West Virginia governor and longtime U.S. senator, has died at age 89. Born into one of America's wealthiest and most prominent families, Rockefeller forged his own path in politics and became a leading voice on healthcare, education and the needs of working families. Lisa Desjardins looks back at Rockefeller's life and impact.

item.title: PBS NewsHour: Sen.-elect Hamilton reflects on why Kansas voters chose a Democrat for U.S. Senate
item.description: Democrats' midterm wins have reached red states across the country, including Kansas, which has not sent a Democrat to the U.S. Senate since 1932. That will soon change after Rev. Adam Hamilton, who leads the largest United Methodist church in the country, defeated Republican incumbent Roger Marshall Tuesday night. Amna Nawaz speaks with Sen.-elect Hamilton for more.

item.title: NPR: American democracy was a big winner in the midterms
item.description: Results are still outstanding House and Senate races but political scientists say one of the big winners in the mid-terms is American democracy itself.

item.title: NPR: What to know about Gina Hinojosa, Texas' first Latina governor-elect
item.description: Gina Hinojosa, state representative from the Rio Grande Valley whose legislative priority has been boosting the public education system, will become the first Latina governor of Texas.

item.title: NPR: Stephen Miller replaces Susie Wiles as White House chief of staff
item.description: White House chief of staff Susie Wiles is being replaced by Stephen Miller, President Trump said Friday. The change comes after Republicans were swept out of power in the midterm elections.

item.title: PBS NewsHour: Seeds and preserved hair in tomb point to oldest signs of cannabis high 2,800 years ago, study suggests
item.description: Archaeologists who led a dig at a monumental tomb in Siberia said they turned up evidence of the earliest known use of cannabis for psychoactive purposes.

item.title: NPR: The economy propelled Democrats to victory. What can they actually do about it?
item.description: Democrats' resounding victory in the midterms can be boiled down to frustrations over the high cost of living and gas prices. But in divided government -- how much can Democrats do?

item.title: PBS NewsHour: Dad of 20-year-old co-pilot in Florida jet crash says her final radio calls showed 'she's tough'
item.description: "I wanted to be by her side," Allan Filgueiras, a pilot who helped teach his daughter to fly, said at a news conference Friday, at times holding back tears. "Inside the plane. To help."

item.title: PBS NewsHour: Cornell faculty vote 'no confidence' in university leadership after alleged fraternity gang rape
item.description: While the faculty body has no power over the university's top leaders, backers of the resolution had said they hoped it would pressure Cornell's trustees to address longstanding institutional failures they identified.

item.title: PBS NewsHour: Democrats win the Arizona House, Senate and governor's office for the first time since 1966
item.description: The Associated Press called enough legislative races to confirm that both chambers flipped on Friday.

item.title: PBS NewsHour: WATCH: 'Elections matter.' Houston mayor limits police cooperation with ICE
item.description: The shift in the nation's fourth-largest city is one of the first actions to restrict U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement operations since Democrats' rout in Tuesday's midterm elections.

item.title: PBS NewsHour: Trump's triumphal arch is blocked for now, but a new website highlights the plans
item.description: The White House highlighted the website the morning after U.S. District Judge Tanya Chutkan issued a temporary restraining order that prohibits work on the site for 14 days.

item.title: NPR: The incoming class of U.S. senators is full of historic firsts
item.description: From the first Native American elected to the U.S. Senate and the first Muslim who will join the upper chamber to the Senate's first Paralympian, voters elected historic candidates in the midterms.

item.title: PBS NewsHour: Connecticut Sen. Chris Murphy released from hospital after stroke
item.description: The 53-year-old Democrat said in a statement Friday that doctors are "encouraged by the progress" he's made so far.

item.title: NPR: No one knows how many ballots are outstanding in Mississippi's Senate race
item.description: The razor-thin margin between GOP Sen. Cindy Hyde-Smith and Democrat Scott Colom is shining a light on an election process in Mississippi that is among the slowest and most decentralized in the U.S.

item.title: PBS NewsHour: Schumer says Democrats will stop Trump from placing 'right-winger' on the Supreme Court
item.description: Schumer says the party's agenda will center around lowering prices, along with five issues that they have focused on in the minority — healthcare, housing, Trump's tariffs, childcare and lowering energy bills.

item.title: PBS NewsHour: Trump names Stephen Miller his next chief of staff after major Republican midterm losses
item.description: President Trump's White House chief of staff, Susie Wiles, is stepping down. She is Trump's longest-serving chief of staff and the first woman ever to hold the position.

item.title: NPR: Stephen Miller will replace Susie Wiles as Trump's chief of staff
item.description: The change comes after sweeping Republican losses in the midterm elections.

item.title: PBS NewsHour: Latino voters propel Democrats to big wins with leftward swing
item.description: Hispanic voters, especially those in the working class, have been impacted by economic challenges, leading them to reject President Donald Trump and his Republican Party.

item.title: NPR: Health intel-sharing group warns industry in wake of cyberattack on French blood bank
item.description: A healthcare intelligence-sharing organization is warning its members to lock down systems following cyberattacks on cold storage systems, including a French blood bank.

item.title: PBS NewsHour: 3 charged in $129 million AI scheme targeting thousands of companies
item.description: Their victims included hospital systems in Missouri and California, a bank in Rhode Island, a financial technology company in the United Kingdom, a mutual fund company in Massachusetts and a pet food company in Florida, according to court documents.

item.title: PBS NewsHour: Online magazine Salon announces it is shutting down
item.description: Salon said there were no immediate plans to take down its online archives, which include three decades of stories from across the world and across topics and genres.

item.title: PBS NewsHour: Opposition to AI data centers in the midterms foreshadows tougher regulations ahead
item.description: Data center regulation itself was not on most midterm ballots, but hard-line stances against the server warehouses were woven into the platforms of Democrats who upended longtime Republican control of the governorships in Texas, Ohio and Georgia, all data center hot spots.

item.title: PBS NewsHour: EU accuses TikTok of violating its digital rules
item.description: The short-video sharing platform must change the design of its "For You" feed so that users have more control over opting out of seeing certain content, the 27-nation bloc's executive arm said Friday.

item.title: PBS NewsHour: Zelenskyy pushes for 'clear' postwar security guarantees in Ukraine
item.description: Zelenskyy emphasized the need for clear, tangible results on paper. Meanwhile, the grim reality of war continues in Ukraine.

item.title: PBS NewsHour: Harmeet Dhillon resigns after radical reshape of Justice Department's Civil Rights Division
item.description: Dhillon has been a powerful and divisive figure inside President Donald Trump's Justice Department since her confirmation last year as assistant attorney general, where she dramatically changed the direction of a division created during the country's Civil Rights Movement to protect the rights of minorities.

item.title: PBS NewsHour: Democratic socialist Nithya Raman defeats Los Angeles Mayor Karen Bass in upset
item.description: The India-born Raman's upstart campaign marked a generational shift at City Hall as voters followed the lead of New York, where democratic socialist Zohran Mamdani was elected last year.

item.title: PBS NewsHour: What to know about Pope Leo XIV's trip to Uruguay, Argentina and Peru
item.description: Pope Leo XIV is returning home to the continent where he spent two decades as a missionary priest and learned to be a pastor, visiting Uruguay, Argentina and his second homeland of Peru.

item.title: PBS NewsHour: Trump's Washington projects are a likely casualty as Democrats claim Congress
item.description: The work his administration is doing to change the physical face of the District of Columbia is sure to encounter far more roadblocks than it did for the first two years of his second term.

item.title: PBS NewsHour: U.S. continues to generate jobs, yet inflation is eroding Americans' spending power
item.description: U.S. employers created a surprising 165,000 new jobs last month, and the unemployment rate dipped to 4.1%.

item.title: PBS NewsHour: AP report: Thomas Markle Sr. arrested on charges related to child sexual abuse material
item.description: The estranged father of Meghan Markle was arrested Friday morning by federal agents in Florida on charges related to child sexual abuse material, two people familiar with the matter told The Associated Press.

item.title: PBS NewsHour: Jay Rockefeller, former West Virginia governor and U.S. senator, dies at 89
item.description: Rockefeller came from one of the nation's richest families to spend a half century in public service in one of the poorest states.

item.title: NPR: Judge halts construction of Trump's arch. And, Labor Department to release jobs report
item.description: A judge has blocked construction of Trump's arch moments after it won federal approval to proceed. And, the Labor Department is set to release the latest jobs report today, a day after stocks plunged.

item.title: NPR: Democrats ran on affordability. What's the party's plan?
item.description: NPR's Leila Fadel asks House Democratic Leader and presumptive House Speaker Hakeem Jeffries about his party's plans to deliver on affordability.

item.title: NPR: Dearborn, Michigan, mayor on city's record turnout and the election of Abdul El-Sayed
item.description: NPR host Leila Fadel speaks with Abdullah Hammoud, the mayor of Dearborn, Michigan, about why his city turned out in record numbers to elect Abdul El-Sayed to the U.S. Senate.

item.title: NPR: Voters under 30 helped drive Tuesday's blue wave
item.description: Young voters played a large role in Democratic wins in this week's midterms. People under 30 voted blue at much higher rates than in 2024.

item.title: NPR: Trump's arch gets a late-night green light. Will a judge stop construction?
item.description: The Trump administration has said it could begin construction immediately after Thursday's vote. All eyes are now on the federal judge who has been asked to block it.

item.title: PBS NewsHour: Alabama executes man for 1991 killings in last of 3 U.S. executions carried out the same day
item.description: Florida carried out a record-tying 19th execution of the year in an unusual instance of three states administering the death penalty on the same day.

item.title: PBS NewsHour: 'JD, habibi.' Arabs celebrate El-Sayed's use of a term of affection in his victory speech
item.description: "Habibi" literally translates to "my beloved" and is peppered through Arab pop songs. In everyday speech, it often means "buddy," "pal," or "bro." El-Sayed's supporters have sported shirts reading "Habibi for Abdul."

item.title: PBS NewsHour: Tankers carrying Russian diesel change course, raising doubts about shipments to U.S.
item.description: President Donald Trump's plan to allow imports of Russian diesel appeared to falter this week after state and federal officials warned that handling any shipments could bring legal consequences and two tankers initially bound for the United States changed course.

item.title: NPR: These are the races in the House and Senate that haven't been called yet
item.description: Democrats are poised to have a strong majority in the upcoming Congress. The final numbers are still being determined. Here's where things stand in the races that are waiting to be called by the AP.

item.title: PBS NewsHour: A look at the midterm races that remain undecided
item.description: As Democrats prepare to take control of Congress and Republicans grapple with stunning losses, every remaining race matters. Some races are still too close to call, including Senate battles in both Alaska and Mississippi. Congressional correspondent Lisa Desjardins reports.

item.title: NPR: Melania Trump touts rare agreement she brokered between Russia and Ukraine
item.description: The six-day pause from the Russian-occupied city of Oleshky comes as the administration ramps up efforts to secure an agreement to end the war in Ukraine.

item.title: PBS NewsHour: News Wrap: Head of Justice Department's civil rights division resigns
item.description: In our news wrap Thursday, Harmeet Dhillon is stepping down as head of the Justice Department's civil rights division, Melania Trump hosted Russian and Ukrainian officials to mark a localized ceasefire and European authorities are investigating a series of bomb threats that targeted more than a dozen flights.

item.title: PBS NewsHour: After midterms, Trump is left to weigh his next move in Iran war that contributed to GOP loss
item.description: As Trump ponders his next move, the stakes couldn't be higher for Iran, the Middle East and the global economy writ large.

item.title: PBS NewsHour: After midterms, world leaders await Trump's next move in Iran
item.description: Tuesday's election results were not just closely watched in the U.S. American elections, in many ways, have become global events and the Democratic wave led to an extraordinary outpouring. Nick Schifrin gauges that reaction.

item.title: PBS NewsHour: Newsom plans to commute all of California's death sentences
item.description: California Gov. Gavin Newsom commuted the state's entire death row population to life in prison without parole. The decision could grant clemency to 548 people. Newsom had previously put a moratorium on executions in the state in 2019, but left hundreds on death row. Amna Nawaz discussed more with Robin Maher of the Death Penalty Information Center.

item.title: PBS NewsHour: Rep. Garcia says voters gave Democrats a mandate to pursue accountability
item.description: With Democrats set to take control of the House, they are making plans to use their majority not only to advance legislation but also to ramp up congressional oversight. California Rep. Robert Garcia is expected to become the new chairman of the House Oversight Committee. He says Democrats have plans to move quickly with a series of investigations. Garcia joined Liz Landers to discuss more.

item.title: PBS NewsHour: Refugee influx and foreign aid cuts strain South Sudan's health care system
item.description: There are few places where the consequences of the Trump administration's cuts to global aid programs are more apparent than South Sudan. With a raging civil war in Sudan to its north, South Sudan is contending not just with its own underserved people, but with more than a million Sudanese refugees. Special correspondent Anna Conkling of Noosphere, a new journalism app, reports.

item.title: PBS NewsHour: State lawmakers seek greater control over what universities can teach
item.description: Democrats in Texas will head to Austin with power they haven't had in decades. One of the many questions is whether they will try to reverse changes made at universities in recent years by Republicans. Texas is not alone. More than half of all college students are enrolled in a state limiting what can be taught or how campuses operate. Stephanie Sy reports for our series, Rethinking College.

item.title: PBS NewsHour: On 'Settle In,' D.L. Hughley recounts his confrontation with Bill Cosby
item.description: D.L. Hughley is one of comedy's most enduring stars. His new memoir, "Charlie's Boy," offers a candid look at fatherhood, family trauma, and the path he took from South Central LA to some of the biggest stages on the planet. Geoff Bennett spoke with Hughley about all that and more, including his heated confrontation with Bill Cosby, on this week's episode of "Settle In."

item.title: NPR: How North Carolina Democrats flipped several House seats in historically GOP districts
item.description: All of these seats were in districts redrawn in 2023 to favor Republican candidates.
